label: XDCR remote cluster reference
type: a registered, named pointer from the local cluster to a remote one - credentials, address and security level - created before any replication and reusable by many. Security is set PER REFERENCE, so changing a reference's security level changes every replication already based on it.
evidence: Once a reference has been registered on the local cluster, it can be specified as the target for a _replication_.
Each replication uses a single _reference_, which has already been created.
Note that replication-security is established _per reference_: this means that the security level assigned applies to all replications based on it.
The source cluster heartbeats are sent as soon as the target remote cluster reference is created on the source cluster.
note: The reference/replication split is the whole architecture of XDCR administration and the registry had neither half. What makes the reference worth a record of its own rather than a field on the replication is the per-reference security scope: it is the unit that security applies to, which means a single edit can silently change the security posture of every replication built on it. That sentence appears once, in a procedure, and is the round's best example of a fact whose owner is the OBJECT rather than the operation.
relates_to_competency_question: What has to exist before an XDCR replication can be created, and what does changing it affect?
